metadata.description:
Case name: Mobil Oil Exploration & Producing Southeast, Inc. v. United States

Opinion filed: 2000-06-26

Docket No.: 99-244

Citations:
• 147 L. Ed. 2d 528
• 120 S. Ct. 2423
• 530 U.S. 604
• 2000 U.S. LEXIS 4306

Case holding summaries:
• "When the United States enters into contract relations, its rights and duties therein are governed generally by the law applicable to contracts between private individuals." (citations omitted)
• “When the United States enters into contract relations, its rights and duties therein are governed generally by the law applicable to contracts between private individuals.”
• holding lease was not subject to later- issued regulation because only future regulations issued under named statutes were incorporated in the text of the lease
• the United States is bound by the same principles of contract law as in contracts between private persons
• "`When the United States enters into contract relations, its rights and duties therein are governed generally by the law applicable to contracts between private individuals.'"
• the United States is bound by the same principles of contract law as in contracts between private persons
• "the fact that Interior's repudiation rested upon the enactment of a new statute makes no significant difference"
• "When the United States enters into contract relations, its rights and duties therein are governed generally by the law applicable to contracts between private individuals."
• relying on Restatement of Contracts for principles of repudiation and restitution
• “The Restatement of Contracts reflects many of the principles of contract law that are applicable to this action.”
• holding that offshore leases issued pursuant to OCSLA are contracts
• “[A]cceptance of performance under a once-repudiated contract can constitute a waiver of the right to restitution that repudiation would otherwise create.”
• stating that acceptance of part performance after repudiation constitutes waiver of restitution damages
• relying similarly on the Restatement of Contracts for principles of repudiation and restitution
